entry.summary: A visitor visa on arrival, generally 31 days. Up to 8 months in total on application.
entry.max_stay: 31 days on arrival; up to 8 months in total on application
entry.pre_arrival: Proof of an onward or return ticket, enough funds and arranged accommodation.
entry.other: With a criminal conviction, contact the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Immigration before travel. Failure to declare can affect future travel.

money-and-cost.currency: Cook Islands dollar (CKD) and New Zealand dollar (NZD)
money-and-cost.cash_card_notes: Cook Islands dollars can only be exchanged in the Cook Islands. Most shops and hotels take cards; ATMs are limited outside Rarotonga and Aitutaki.

laws.rule: Severe penalties for even small amounts of illegal drugs. A personal supply of a controlled drug (for example methylphenidate for ADHD, codeine or morphine) has specific legal requirements: check with the Ministry of Health before travel.

Sale and import of vapes and e-cigarettes are banned. Visitors over 21 may bring one device and up to 30 ml of e-liquid, and must take it with them or surrender it to the Ministry of Health on departure.
Drive on an Australian licence for up to 6 months, only vehicles your licence covers. A scooter needs a temporary motorbike licence: a practical test at police headquarters in Avarua.

culture-and-protocol.dress_and_conduct: Modest dress and behaviour, especially outside resorts, in villages and on the outer islands. Visitors are welcome at Sunday services: shirts and long trousers for men, longer skirts or dresses for women, shoulders covered.
culture-and-protocol.cultural_authority: Ask locally: your host, or the island's own people, on each island.
culture-and-protocol.note: Read from the Australian Government's description of local customs.

seasons-and-flow.notes: The wet season runs late November to April or May, about a month longer at Rarotonga. Visitor flow (peak and quiet months) is still to be read from the tourism authority's statistics.
